title: Hall's Theorem: Hall Subgroups in Finite Solvable Groups
description: Formalizes Hall's theorem (Philip Hall, 1928): in a finite solvable group G, for every Hall divisor d of |G| — meaning d | |G| and gcd(d, |G|/d) = 1 — there exists a subgroup of order d. This is the strongest converse to Lagrange's theorem, characterizing solvability. Proves the cyclic case via orderOf_pow' and IsCyclic.exists_generator, the prime case via Cauchy's theorem, and axiomatizes the general solvable case with a full proof sketch.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: hall_solvable: Hall's theorem for solvable groups (requires Schur–Zassenhaus + minimal normal subgroup theory not yet in Mathlib). hall_characterizes_solvability: Hall's converse (requires Feit–Thompson odd-order theorem).
originalContributions: IsHallDivisor definition: d | n with gcd(d, n/d) = 1, the formal Hall divisor condition
IsHallSubgroup definition: subgroup H with gcd(|H|, [G:H]) = 1
hall_cyclic: Hall's theorem for cyclic groups proved via orderOf_pow' — zpowers(g^(n/d)) has order d
hall_prime_div: prime-order Hall subgroups via Cauchy's theorem (exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card)
hall_trivial_bot and hall_trivial_top: trivial Hall subgroup cases (d=1 and d=|G|)
hall_solvability_necessary: A₅ (order 60) is not solvable; 15 = Hall divisor of 60 has no realizing subgroup
Numerical examples: Hall divisors of 12 (only 1,3,4,12) and 30 (all divisors)
meta.proofStrategy: Part I: Define IsHallDivisor (d|n ∧ gcd(d,n/d)=1) and IsHallSubgroup (gcd(|H|,[G:H])=1). Part II: Prove cyclic case via orderOf_pow' — for generator g of order n, zpowers(g^(n/d)) has order d using Nat.gcd_eq_right and Nat.div_div_self. Part III: Prime case via Cauchy (exists_prime_orderOf_dvd_card). Part IV: Axiomatize general solvable case with proof sketch: induct on |G|, use minimal normal subgroup N (elementary abelian p-group), split on p|d or p∤d, apply Schur–Zassenhaus.

openQuestions.question: Can the full proof of Hall's theorem be formalized in Lean 4 without using Schur–Zassenhaus as a black box, by building the minimal normal subgroup induction from scratch?
Does Mathlib have Schur–Zassenhaus (existence of complements to normal Hall subgroups)? If so, can Hall's theorem be proved with 0 axioms?

sections.title: Hall Divisors
sections.description: A Hall divisor d of n is a divisor with gcd(d, n/d) = 1. Hall divisors correspond to subsets of prime factors of n — the primes dividing d are disjoint from those dividing n/d.

sections.title: Cyclic Case (Proved)
sections.description: For cyclic G with generator g of order n, the subgroup ⟨g^(n/d)⟩ has order d. This is proved using orderOf_pow' which gives orderOf(g^k) = n/gcd(n,k), and Nat.gcd_eq_right to simplify when d | n.

sections.title: General Solvable Case (Axiom)
sections.description: The full Hall's theorem is axiomatized. The proof sketch: induct on |G|, take minimal normal N ≅ (ℤ/pℤ)^k, split cases on p | d or p ∤ d, and apply Schur–Zassenhaus to lift Hall subgroups from G/N back to G.

sections.title: Sharpness: A₅ Counterexample
sections.description: 15 is a Hall divisor of 60 = |A₅|, but A₅ has no subgroup of order 15. This proves solvability is necessary in Hall's theorem.
